chunks: Ali ibn Asbat from Abu Makhlad al-Sarraj said:

I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when Mu'tib entered and said, 'There are two men at the door.' He said, 'Bring them in.' So they entered, and one of them said, 'I am a tanner; I sell leopard skins.' He asked, 'Are they tanned?' He said, 'Yes.' He said, 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.لَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ: There is no harm in it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell tanned leopard skins in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the practical application of the principle that tanning purifies the hide of an animal, even if it is not slaughtered according to Islamic rites, thereby rendering its trade permissible. The specific mention of the seller as a 'Sarraj' (leather worker) highlights the professional context of the inquiry, while the Imam’s concise ruling underscores the ease and accessibility of commercial laws in Shia jurisprudence. This establishes a clear precedent for the permissibility of selling tanned hides of non-Muslim slaughtered animals, a key distinction in Usuli fiqh.
